hook.text: A scream, a laugh, a sigh—these sounds carry meaning instantly without a single word.

buildup.text: Emotional vocalizations are ancient. Dogs, birds, and reptiles all signal fear and aggression vocally.

discovery.text: Humans still use non-verbal sounds constantly: gasps, groans, and 'hmm' fill our conversations.

twist.text: These emotional signals are processed in older brain regions, separate from language areas.

climax.text: Language was built on top of an emotional sound system that was already millions of years old.

punchline.text: Feelings had a voice long before thoughts did.

quiz.question: How do emotional vocalizations relate to language?
options: Language was built on top of older emotional sound systems
